doc.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001

title: Closing remarks and goodbyes
summary: Rowe thanks May, offers a possible Part Two, and they joke about playing together.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: You know, I remember— That’s fantastic. Well I’ve enjoyed talking to you immensely.
Is there anything that I should have asked you that maybe I haven’t? That maybe you’d like to throw in here?
I can’t think of anything off hand. Now when I leave here, I’ll go oh, darnit.
Well we’ll do Part Two. We’ve done that in the past—.
Well I’ll give you a call if I think there’s something. I hope this turns out good because I’m usually not too good at this kind of thing.
Yeah? Well I think it was fine. So thanks for your time. I really appreciate it.
Thank you very, very much. It was a great pleasure to meet you. Maybe we’ll get a chance to play some.
That’d be great. I would look forward to that immensely.
If we ever come up to your school, will you play with us?
Yes, I will. I’ll be nervous like you were with Coltrane though, okay?
I’ll bet you won’t because we’ll make you feel so comfortable. I’ll bet you won’t be nervous. I guarantee.
